sql_exec.name: sql_exec
sql_exec.description:
Run one agent-written read-only analytical query over the warehouse.

The query must be a single SELECT or WITH statement over the declared
silver tables. Writes, stacked statements, and tables outside the
declared set are refused before execution. DESCRIBE, SHOW TABLES,
information_schema and catalog functions are refused as well; call
warehouse_schema for table and column listings. Results are capped at
RERUN_ROW_CAP rows with a RERUN_TIMEOUT_S statement timeout; a valid
query returning 0 rows returns ok=True, rows=[], row_count=0, and
meta.empty_observation=True (unless DIME_STRICT_NONEMPTY_SQL=1).
Name the primary numeric column for what it measures, so a percentage
answers as TS_PCT and a count as `n`; the column you alias is the
column a citation binds to.

Every ok result also carries meta.basis and meta.profile. If you need
a contributor count for an expression such as AVG, or distinct-value
counts, add COUNT(metric) or COUNT(DISTINCT x) columns to your query.

sql.description: DuckDB SELECT query over the warehouse tables.
sql.title: Sql

Optional "sign_and_trade" = {"player":"...","new_salary":15000000,"years":3} (positive salary, 3-4 season term, BYC handled; first-season full guarantee required by 2023 CBA Art. VII sec. 8(e)(1) is not validated; prior-team and preseason eligibility not modeled; years is treated as total declared seasons; non-option seasons cannot be distinguished, so option-year treatment is unsupported), "cash" = [{"from","to","amount"}] with positive integer amounts between trade parties, "tpe" = [{"team","amount","kind":"ordinary|sign_and_trade","origin_season":"YYYY-YY","origin_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","expiry_date":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]; rows are declared uses, not inventory. TPE kind is optional: ordinary accepts the standard alias, and sign_and_trade accepts sign_and_trade_generated, snt and snt_generated. Use origin_season in consecutive-year YYYY-YY form or origin_year as the season-start year; they must agree if both are present. Optional origin_date and expiry_date use YYYY-MM-DD exact dates; origin_date uses the July-June league-year calendar, must agree with origin_year/origin_season when both are supplied, and derives a one-year expiry when expiry_date is omitted. Explicit expiry_date must be after origin_date. Present keys must be non-null, and amount/origin_year must be JSON integers, so bool/float values are rejected. Amount-only legacy rows default to ordinary current-season uses and return legacy_defaults. Optional evaluation_date is YYYY-MM-DD and defaults to the league date in America/New_York. Exact expiry deadlines remain usable through their dates and expire only afterward; weekend and federal-holiday deadlines roll to the following business day. Season-only rows keep conservative legacy season bins and are explicitly approximate. At season grain, current and prior season origins are active, older entries expire, and future entries are unavailable. Each active row is a separate amount+$250k capacity bin, with the cushion reduced to $0 over the first apron. TPEs cannot combine with player salary or each other for one acquisition. Outgoing first-round picks are duplicate-checked and validated at year grain against silver_future_picks when seeded; protection/swap reconciliation and pooled/conditional picks are not modeled; same-year multiple firsts are validated only at year grain because the leg input does not identify the original team of a same-year first. Checks 2023 CBA salary matching tiers, apron aggregation bans, post-trade hard caps, typed TPE restrictions, cash bans, the frozen second-apron pick, and Stepien consecutive-first rules. REACH FOR THIS for any trade-legality ask beyond a trivial two-team player swap: sign-and-trade, multi-team, picks/Stepien, apron aggregation, TPE or cash involved. For a simple two-team salary match get_trade_check is enough. Payroll/apron values use the warehouse salary ledger as a proxy for exact Apron Team Salary; bonus, dead-money, roster-status, exception-inventory, free-agent/tender, and offseason adjustments are not computable, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. search_game_logs.name: search_game_logs
search_game_logs.description:
Filter game logs by stat thresholds, opponent, time, or home/away.

player: name, nickname, or id (same resolution as every other tool).
Required unless league_wide=True or team_wide=True.
league_wide: when True, ignore player and return per-player match
counts across the whole warehouse (answers "who had the most
50-point games this season").
team_wide: when True, ignore player and return per-team match
counts across the whole warehouse (answers "which team had the
most 50-point games this season"). Each matched game counts for
the team the player was on that night (first token of MATCHUP,
e.g. "LAL vs. BOS" -> "LAL"), so a mid-season trade attributes
each game to the team at game time, not the current team.
playoffs: when True, read silver_playoff_gamelogs instead of the
regular-season table.
min_points / min_rebounds / min_assists: per-game stat floors
(e.g. min_points=40 for 40-point games). min_pra: points + rebounds
+ assists floor. max_points / max_rebounds / max_assists: per-game
stat ceilings, exclusive (max_points=20 keeps 0-19 games -
"under 20"). triple_double / double_double: keep only games
with 10+ in 3 (or 2) of PTS/REB/AST/STL/BLK. opponent: team name or
abbreviation, e.g. "Knicks" or "NYK". month: name, number, or
YYYY-MM. start_date / end_date: YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. home_away:
"home" or "away". season: 2025-26 only in the warehouse.
best_game: when True, ignore the limit and return only the single
highest-scoring game (answers "best game" / "career high" phrasing).
Returns matching games, most recent first, with the total match
count (rows beyond limit are counted, not returned). A player with
no rows in the chosen scope is an explicit ok:False error, never a
silent 0.
Warehouse only; 2025-26 only.
